comparator.name: Public Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The live 2026-2027 Leiden Study Guide identifies three formal 180-EC Public Administration routes. The generic target is represented by Policy, Public Administration, and Organisation because it most broadly covers the programme's public-administration identity across policy, institutions, organisations, management, law, politics, sociology, economics and research methods; the choice is independent of UCR fit. The route totals 60 EC in each year. Years 1 and 2 each contain twelve compulsory 5-EC courses. Year 3 contains a 15-EC bachelor thesis, three compulsory 5-EC courses and 30 EC of genuine elective space. The zero-credit mentorship and legacy cohort-only modules are omitted.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Public Administration target does not name a route. Of Leiden's three current formal routes, Policy, Public Administration, and Organisation most broadly represents public administration through policy formation and implementation, public organisations and management, political and legal institutions, economics, mixed methods, leadership and a thesis. Economics, Public Administration, and Management and Digitalisation, Governance and Society are more specialised directions.

alternatives.label: Public policy, governance and organisations
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates politics, law, sociology, economics, organisational leadership, policy questions and mixed research methods around public institutions and decisions.
alternatives.concept: A broad public-administration programme examining how governments and public organisations make, justify and implement decisions. Political science, law, sociology, economics, leadership and communication are combined with quantitative, qualitative and independent research.
progression: Foundations in comparative politics, sociology, economics, research and communication precede advanced public economics, organisational leadership, constitutional and international law, EU politics and independent research. Law, Society & Justice precedes both upper-level law courses; Research Methods & Statistics precedes all courses that require it. Every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Economic governance and public management
alternatives.labelReason: Economics, econometrics, public finance, business governance and management organise a distinct route around the economic design and management of public decisions.
alternatives.concept: Focuses on how economic institutions, incentives, public finance, organisations and management shape government choices. Economics and econometrics are integrated with politics, law, sociology, strategy, leadership and qualitative research.
progression: Economics, politics, sociology, research and business foundations precede public economics, strategy, business law, international governance, econometrics and market research. Research Methods & Statistics and Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precede every course that formally requires them. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad policy route, this programme replaces human rights, modern sociology, international law, sustainability governance, persuasive communication, peace and conflict, and history research with business foundations, macroeconomics, digital strategy, transnational business law, international business governance, econometrics and market research. Seven courses differ in each direction, and the changes follow the economic-governance concept.

alternatives.label: Digital governance, data and responsible AI
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, data science, AI ethics and AI decision-making form a distinct technical strand joined to law, politics, organisational change and public accountability.
alternatives.concept: Examines how data, algorithms and artificial intelligence transform public decisions, organisations and citizen-state relations. Technical foundations in programming, data science and AI are combined with ethics, law, politics, sociology, leadership and governance research.
progression: Programming, introductory data science, comparative politics and research methods precede AI decision-making, machine learning, AI optimisation, constitutional and international law, organisational leadership and independent research. Introduction to Programming, Law, Society & Justice, and Research Methods & Statistics precede all courses that formally require them. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this programme replaces economics, ethics, human rights, modern and advanced sociology, microeconomics, persuasive communication with programming, data science, AI ethics, AI decision-making, machine learning, media and race, and AI optimisation. Seven courses differ in each direction. It differs from the economic-governance route by eleven courses in each direction, reflecting its data-and-AI rather than economics-and-management priority.

Public organisations, management and economic governance
Both examine organisational behaviour, leadership, groups and culture.
Both address organisational management; UCR supplies general business foundations rather than dedicated public management.
Both study public economics, market failure and government intervention.
Both introduce social research design and quantitative analysis.

selection.assessment: The broad closest route covers the public-administration, policy, institutional, organisational, legal and research core. The target's current formal routes and direct interests independently support an economics-and-management programme and a digital-government, data and responsible-AI programme. All three concepts are coherent and feasible. The closest and economic routes differ by seven courses in each direction, the closest and digital routes by seven, and the economic and digital routes by eleven, so every pair exceeds the 30-EC distinctness floor. Three is the maximum.

notes.text: Leiden provides a dedicated Public Administration sequence with route-specific policy, organisation, economics or digital-government courses and a 15-EC thesis. UCR can build three coherent 24-course programmes from politics, law, sociology, economics, leadership, data science, AI and research methods, but it does not reproduce the same continuous disciplinary sequence; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
